knobs.name: capture_twice

L2-1: sysTester.DirListing event 2 names P and no other file

knobs.mechanism: CAPTURE is sent twice in a row; two products are written where the test expects one

knobs.name: corrupt_first_product

L2-2: the two sysTester.Sha256 events of P1 carry the same hash

knobs.mechanism: sysTester.CORRUPT_PRODUCT(P1) is inserted before the second DUMP_SHA256 of P1: the first two bytes of its picture record are overwritten on board, as an overwriting second capture would; the teardown removes the product

knobs.name: corrupt_in_transfer

L5-5:
sha256 of record/raw/files/

== hash in the first sysTester.Sha256 event of P
the two sysTester.Sha256 events of P carry the same hash

knobs.mechanism: sysTester.CORRUPT_PRODUCT(P) is inserted before DOWNLINK(P), after the first DUMP_SHA256: the product sent and kept differs from the product hashed; the transfer still runs, so the test's preconditions hold

knobs.name: delete_other

L2-4: the two sysTester.Sha256 events of P2 carry the same hash

knobs.mechanism: DELETE(P1) is sent as DELETE(P2), the product named by the preceding DUMP_SHA256; the wrong product is removed, and the second DUMP_SHA256 of P2 fails on a missing file

knobs.name: downlink_existing

L6-1: exactly one command fails (cmdDisp.OpCodeError) and it is the rejected DOWNLINK; every other command completes
ground CFDP transactions in the window: none

knobs.mechanism: DOWNLINK(Dp_missing.fxd) is sent with the name of the test's own product, taken from the preceding DUMP_SHA256 command; the product is sent

knobs.name: second_capture_dropped

L5-1: exactly one command fails (cmdDisp.OpCodeError) and it is the rejected CAPTURE; every other command completes

knobs.mechanism: LIST_PRODUCTS (accepted during a capture) is sent in place of the second CAPTURE; no command is rejected
